subject: Physics
subtopic: Direction recovery, i/j notation and 2-D unit direction
axis_note: Owner-approved ExamSIDE preparation-demand matrix implementing the bounded production sequence from the merged Vector reconnaissance. It does not include dot/cross/3-D/calculus depth.

must_contain: Signed x/y components in declared axes.

controlled_variation.notice: reference angle can stay the same while physical quadrant changes
the vertical-axis special case replaces division by Ax

must_contain: A component pair and its exact i-hat/j-hat translation.
A round-trip recovery of the signed pair.

controlled_variation.notice: only the corresponding basis coefficient sign changes

controlled_variation.vary: notation from pair to i/j form
controlled_variation.notice: representation changes while the vector does not

must_contain: A nonzero 2-D vector in component/i-j form.

controlled_variation.vary: overall positive scale of the original vector

controlled_variation.notice: the unit vector preserves the changed physical direction

family.invariant_demand: Retain component signs, translate representations without changing the vector, and normalize by one common magnitude while checking physical direction.
family.difficult_move: Separating reference angle from physical direction and treating i/j notation/normalization as representation operations rather than new force or motion laws.
family.independent_check: Direction must reproduce component signs; i/j translation must round-trip; a unit vector must have magnitude one and rescale back to the original vector.

support_ladder.handed_over: Axes, sign pair and target representation are named.
Axes and components are supplied; learner chooses the conversion/check.
Only the vector data and requested direction/notation/unit direction are supplied.

transfer.changed_demand: A resultant is given only as signed components and the question asks for direction.
A vector written as a pair must be used in i/j notation or vice versa.
A question asks only for direction as a unit vector, not the original magnitude.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: the common normalization scale and magnitude-one check
